A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HO-SFL research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–C are readable and can be reliably matched across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision and language experiments, communication and memory measurements, a latency simulation, and client-depth and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds SQuAD fine-tuning results across four model configurations.

M1.justification: The Lagrangian formulation, server backpropagation, client zeroth-order estimator, scalar aggregation, and synchronization procedures in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged. Larger-model evaluation and discussion of possible privacy defenses do not introduce an implemented method component.

E1.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 add SQuAD generative reading comprehension, extending evaluation from image classification and language classification/coreference to generated answers. This introduces a distinct task regime while retaining all previous datasets and IID/non-IID coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding vision comparisons retain SFL, FSL-SAGE, ZO-SFL, and MU-SplitFed; the existing language comparisons retain SplitLoRA and ZO-SFL. The new SQuAD experiment uses the already evaluated SplitLoRA comparator. Newly discussed prior methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added SQuAD experiment introduces F1 evaluation and extends model configurations to LLaMA-3.2-3B and Qwen3-8B, each assigning five transformer layers to clients. Existing experiments retain their budgets, participation settings, optimizers, LoRA configuration, and data partitions.

E4.justification: The latency-feasibility simulation and client-depth, perturbation-count, and smoothing-parameter analyses in Appendix C are unchanged. The added SQuAD table supplies benchmark results across models without a separate new ablation, robustness test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Ten-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting for the vision experiments and hyperparameter ablations is retained. The new SQuAD table reports point estimates, following the existing language-results presentation; no new run counts, uncertainty procedures, or significance tests are disclosed.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports HO-SFL/SplitLoRA SQuAD F1 scores of 0.5744/0.5985 for OPT-125M, 0.8687/0.8804 for LLaMA-1B, 0.9238/0.9271 for LLaMA-3B, and 0.9389/0.9413 for Qwen3-8B. Existing numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Assumptions 4.1–4.2, Proposition 4.3, Theorem 4.4, Corollary 4.5, and all definitions and proofs in Appendix A are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about backpropagation-free clients, dimension-free aggregation, convergence, and memory efficiency. The additional experiments support the existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: New Section 6 discusses activation-inversion risks, possible differential-privacy defenses, relationships to checkpointing and shallow splitting, and selecting perturbation counts within the latency-hiding window. Section 5.2 additionally interprets the SQuAD scores as evidence of robust scaling without convergence degradation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Code Availability statement with an implementation-repository link. Appendix B adds SQuAD partition sizes and the total/client layer counts for the two larger models. Existing implementation and profiling details remain unchanged; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 newly distinguishes HO-SFL's model-split hybridization from Talaei et al.'s hybrid decentralized optimization. References for SQuAD, Qwen3, and differential-private split learning are also added. Other reference changes primarily update metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: v2 adds Discussions, Acknowledgements, and Code Availability sections, revises selected related-work and experimental paragraphs, and updates affiliation and publication text. The existing narrative, methodology, and appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the SQuAD results table, shifts surrounding text and Table 1, and renumbers the appendix tables. The vision-table heading changes from SFL-ZO to ZO-SFL. All eight figures retain their graphics, axes, legends, and captions.

improvement.justification: The SQuAD results extend empirical support to generated answers and 3B/8B models, while the privacy discussion and implementation link improve transparency. These provide useful, bounded gains over v1. However, Table 2's final F1 scores do not establish the claimed absence of convergence degradation, and the proposed differential-privacy integration remains unvalidated.
